title: Total iron-binding capacity (TIBC)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: Total iron-binding capacity (TIBC) is an iron test that measures how well iron attaches to transferrin and other proteins in the blood. It is one of several tests used to check iron levels in the body.
context: TIBC is usually read together with other iron tests to understand iron levels. A result outside the usual range does not always mean a condition that needs care, and some medicines, such as birth control pills and estrogen, can affect iron levels.
aboveRange: A higher result may be associated with low iron levels in the body, which can be a sign of anemia
belowRange: A lower result may be associated with high iron levels in the body, such as iron overload (hemochromatosis)
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
